extracted.intended_audience: hospital administrators, hospital legal/compliance teams, physician-owned hospitals, ASC operators, health policy stakeholders, and commenters to CMS
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and questions for stakeholders on proposed and existing Medicare episode-based payment models (TEAM, CJR/CJR-X) and related provider-based and physician-ownership regulatory criteria, including requests for comment on participation, waivers, quality measures, and location tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing ASC inclusion in TEAM
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions to evaluate whether to include ambulatory surgery centers (ASCs) in TEAM focusing on appropriate beneficiary-level risk adjustment and site-of-service decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS asks: How should beneficiary-level risk adjustment methodology be adapted to ensure appropriate site-of-service decisions? Could including ASCs in TEAM create barriers to care for any Medicare beneficiaries? What could CMS do to mitigate this?

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling model overlap
rubrics_metrics.description: Considerations for how TEAM ASC episodes should overlap or interact with other value-based care initiatives or payment models focused on the same procedures at ASCs or hospitals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS requests comments on how to handle TEAM ASC episode overlap with other value-based care initiatives or payment models focused on the same procedures at either ASCs or hospitals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality measures for TEAM ASC episodes
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine quality measures that would reasonably capture performance and outcomes of TEAM ASC episodes and metrics for fair comparison between ASCs and hospital outpatient departments (HOPDs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions include: What quality measures would reasonably capture performance and outcomes of TEAM ASC episodes? On what quality metrics can ASCs and hospital outpatient departments be fairly compared? What opportunities exist for quality improvement at ASCs for procedures included in (or suggested for inclusion in) TEAM?

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a hospital with physician ownership (POH)
rubrics_metrics.description: A hospital in which a physician, or an immediate family member of a physician, has an ownership or investment interest in the hospital, including equity, debt, or an interest in an entity that holds an interest in the hospital.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text clarifies ownership may be through equity, debt, or other means and includes interests in entities that hold interests in the hospital; estimated >250 acute care hospitals have physician ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stark law (section 1877) prohibitions and exception authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1877 prohibits a physician from making referrals for certain designated health services payable by Medicare to an entity with which he/she (or immediate family) has a financial relationship unless an applicable exception is satisfied, and prohibits the entity from filing claims for improperly referred services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A financial relationship may be ownership/investment interest or a compensation arrangement. The statute establishes specific exceptions and grants the HHS Secretary authority to create regulatory exceptions for relationships that do not pose program or patient abuse risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rural provider exception requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To use the rural provider exception (section 1877(d)(2)), an entity must furnish substantially all of the designated health services it furnishes to residents of a rural area (as defined in section 1886(d)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For hospitals, to satisfy requirements the hospital must meet section 1877(i)(1) of the Act no later than September 23, 2011. These exceptions are codified at §411.356(c)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Whole hospital exception requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Whole hospital exception (section 1877(d)(3)) applies for ownership or investment interests in a hospital located outside Puerto Rico if: the referring physician is authorized to perform services at the hospital; the interest is in the hospital itself (not a subdivision); and the hospital met section 1877(i)(1) by the statutory cutoff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codified at §411.356(c)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of ACA Section 6001(a) on physician-ownership exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 6001(a) of the Affordable Care Act effectively eliminated the exceptions for physician ownership/investment in hospitals, except that hospitals with physician ownership/investment and a Medicare provider agreement on December 31, 2010, are grandfathered and may continue to use the rural provider or whole hospital exception if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 6001(a)(3) amended rural/whole hospital exceptions to prohibit increasing operating rooms, procedure rooms, and beds beyond levels licensed on March 23, 2010 (or relevant effective provider agreement date), although the Secretary may grant an exception from the prohibition on facility expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program integrity concerns with POHs
rubrics_metrics.description: POHs raise concerns similar to physician self-referral law risks — overutilization, patient steering, cherry-picking, and lemon-dropping — which justify limits on POH expansion under current law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS notes evidence both raising concerns and suggesting POHs may help control costs, maintain/improve outcomes, and prevent consolidation. Comments/analysis should weigh these competing considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardrails for voluntary POH participation in TEAM
rubrics_metrics.description: If CMS permits voluntary opt-in for POHs to TEAM, guardrails must be in place to prevent self-selection bias, losses to Medicare, and threats to evaluation integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS cites prior parameters (e.g., voluntary participants limited to certain strata and inhibited from voluntary exit; required participation in all episode categories) and anticipates similar parameters for any future voluntary participation opportunities to ensure model integrity and minimize losses to Medicare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and inclusion criteria for POHs opting into TEAM
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions on whether POHs opting into TEAM should be limited to those grandfathered under ACA exceptions, required to meet geographic eligibility in 42 CFR 512.515, and be subject to participation requirements in 42 CFR 512.510; requests suggestions for additional inclusion criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS requests comment on which inclusion criteria, if any, should be added for POHs opting to participate in TEAM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic waivers necessary for POH participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify programmatic waivers (for example, restrictions on expansion of facility capacity, service limitations) that may be necessary to ensure POHs can successfully participate in TEAM, with justification and explanation of how the waiver will not undermine the TEAM model or allow Medicare payment where not currently allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waivers of law, if provided and necessary to test a model, are temporary and generally end when the model expires or the participant's agreement is terminated. CMS asks for justification and explanation of safeguards to prevent undermining the model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-waiver transition and compliance assurances for POHs
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans and safeguards to ensure POHs continue any successful actions taken under TEAM once they must comply with all applicable statutes/regulations (including physician self-referral law) after model termination or waiver end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example question: If TEAM waives Section 6001(a)(3) to allow POH expansion beyond baseline operating rooms/procedure rooms/beds, how can CMS ensure the POH reduces facility capacity back to baseline as required by regulations (e.g., 42 CFR 411.362(b)(2), 411.363(a))?

rubrics_metrics.name: Program integrity requirements to prevent beneficiary harm
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional program integrity requirements CMS should consider to avoid beneficiary steering, cherry-picking, and lemon-dropping and ensure beneficiary choice is not compromised if waivers are offered to POHs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS asks for suggestions on additional integrity safeguards to protect beneficiaries and program integrity when offering waivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of episode categories or services for POHs
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether any episode categories should be excluded from episode initiation, or any items and services should be excluded from target prices for POHs in TEAM, and provide evidence to support such exclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS requests evidence-backed proposals for exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider-based location criteria and risk of overpayment
rubrics_metrics.description: Rationale for clear criteria distinguishing provider-based facilities from freestanding facilities to avoid improper increased Medicare payments and increased beneficiary coinsurance liability without commensurate program or beneficiary benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: History of Program Memoranda and regulations at 42 CFR 413.65; CMS emphasizes importance of clear criteria for acquiring provider-based status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Same patient population location tests (§413.65(e)(3)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: To satisfy the location criterion a facility must demonstrate during the immediately preceding 12-month period either: (A) at least 75% of the patients served by the facility reside in the same zip code areas as at least 75% of the patients served by the main provider; or (B) at least 75% of the patients served by the facility who required the type of care furnished by the main provider received that care from the main provider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §413.65(e)(3)(iv) provides a temporary test for newly established facilities without 12 months of data. CMS expresses concerns about application of test (B) to inpatient facilities and notes the example of referral relationships was intended for isolated outpatient facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limiting the referral-based 75% test to outpatient facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to revise §413.65(e)(3)(iii)(B) to specify it applies only to outpatient departments; inpatient facilities would be excluded from utilizing the referral-based 75% test to meet the location requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS rationale: allowing the referral-based exception for inpatient facilities could permit hospitals to obtain unwarranted payment advantages for inpatient services provided at considerable distances; outpatient test preserves original intent to permit outpatient locations to exceed 35-mile radius in certain isolated circumstances. CMS also proposes clarifying language at §413.65(e)(3)(iii)(A) to make explicit that provision may be used by inpatient or outpatient facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory findings required to expand a model nationwide (section 1115A(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Before expanding a tested model nationwide, the Secretary must find: (1) expansion is expected to reduce spending without reducing quality of care or improve quality without increasing spending; (2) the CMS Chief Actuary certifies expansion would reduce or not increase net program spending; and (3) expansion would not deny or limit coverage or provision of benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS applies these three findings in proposing to expand CJR to CJR-X and cites evaluation evidence and Chief Actuary certification supporting the findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and spending metrics for evaluating CJR/CJR-X
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation metrics used to determine whether the model maintained quality while reducing spending include ED visits, unplanned readmission rates, mortality rates, LEJR complication rates, and aggregate net savings and statistical significance of savings/losses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS cites evaluation results (e.g., $112.7 million net savings across PYs 6 and 7 while maintaining quality) and notes earlier PYs where COVID-era adjustments produced statistically significant losses; these outcomes inform policy decisions on expansion and model modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design elements proposed for CJR-X
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed CJR-X would expand CJR to all eligible acute care hospitals nationwide and incorporate policy changes informed by CJR and TEAM lessons: inclusion of outpatient episodes, updated target price methodology, more comprehensive risk adjustment, and protections for safety net and low-volume hospitals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposes codifying CJR-X policies at §§512.600–512.695 and exempting TEAM participant hospitals (that include LEJR episode) from CJR-X until the end of TEAM model test.
